residency: Overlay, model and mapped pages retained across cases; firmware reloaded and verified before every boot; each case starts with cache-valid length zero.
eos_policy: EOS is an ordinary selected token; produce the requested fixed count with lowest-ID greedy ties.
warmup: First story cached-decode interval is retained but excluded from the three-sample summary.
measured_samples: The next three consecutive story cached-decode intervals. Context grows by one each time; these are not repeated identical-context trials.
primary_boundary: Resident host START through safe RETURN_CPU and copying generated token IDs. Includes cache ownership synchronization, firmware initialization, prefill/decode, metadata, packing, transfers, KV, logits, selection and output delivery; excludes independent checks.
firmware_ttft: Firmware model-loop entry through publication and fence of the first selected token. This is token-ready time in DDR, not interactive host TTFT.
decode_boundary: Previous token publication timestamp through the next token publication and fence, including cached forward and greedy selection.
prefill_forward: Forward-only subinterval recorded separately; the complete initial step including selection is firmware TTFT.
profiling: Cycle timestamps and aggregate counters in all cases; five selected trace copies during story prefill only. Trace cost remains in the observed prefill/generation timings.
statistics_limit: Three measured decode samples are descriptive, not a tail-latency or endurance estimate.
startup: Record one provisioning observation separately. Do not claim repeated cold-start or disk-cold measurements.
comparison: Historical M4 results only with explicit hardware/workload differences; no paired-speedup claim from unmatched contexts.
